newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Farm ministers agree tighter flax aid controls.
newsitem.headline: Farm ministers agree tighter flax aid controls.

text.p: European Union farm ministers approved on Monday new controls to ensure that flax subsidies are only paid to farmers who sell their crop, EU diplomats said.
The controls follow a 30 percent increase to 134,133 hectares in the EU flax area in the 1996/97 crop year and a 70 percent rise since 1989/90.
EU aid payable to flax producers in 1996/97 totals just over 116 million Ecus, given an aid rate of 865.48 Ecus per hectare.
"The controls were agreed unanimously after Spain gained a concession," said one diplomat.
The European Commission said it had no objections to a Spanish request to remove an obligation for farmers to achieve minimum flax yields per hectare in order to qualify for subsidies.
Diplomats said that the new controls were aimed at stopping farmers growing flax only to obtain EU subsidies.
The biggest increase has been in Spain where the planted area has surged to 46,613 hectares in 1996/97, from zero in 1992/93.
The British area has also rose sharply to to 17,700 hectares in 1994, from 2,200 ha the previous year but British officials said that production was all marketed.
France, Belgium and the Netherlands are the main traditional flax producers. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
